protections: Adjacent inline text runs are merged in amortized-linear time: text is appended into the surviving Text node (Text::append / InlineParserEngine::addPlainText) instead of re-copying a growing accumulator.
A block-level attribute list that spans several continuation lines is accumulated so that the stored attribute set is not re-serialized and re-copied on every line.
Inline attribute nodes that all target one element are merged and filtered once per target, with work proportional to the attributes actually added rather than to the accumulated set.
Resolving the target of an inline attribute node is bounded, instead of re-walking the whole run of adjacent attribute nodes once per node.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The cleanup only replaces a Quote with a Text and merges at most two neighbours, and the copying lives in a shared core helper (AdjacentTextMerger) that also runs on the normal parse path, so the helper looks already linear.

Each dash/ellipsis run is consumed in one match and the engine appends following plain text into the last Text node, so the node count per line looks bounded; the append guard in addPlainText is assumed to keep the tree flat, but these parsers append Text nodes directly and never call it.

A multi-line attribute block is a documented convenience feature that normally has two or three lines; each merge looks like a small array operation, and the class value must stay a space-joined string because that shape is asserted by the unit tests.

The DocumentParsedEvent listener runs once per attribute node and the block parser is assumed to have already merged the attributes, so this reads as one cheap copy rather than a full rebuild of the accumulated set (merge plus allowlist filter) for every node.

Each attribute node is detached as it is processed and the loop breaks at the first neighbour that is not an attribute node, so the walk looks amortized; it is only quadratic when the attribute run sits at the start of a container (heading content, emphasis or link label) so that a processed node leaves its successor with no previous sibling.

masking: T1 masks T2: rewriting the quote cleanup to a single merge pass still runs through AdjacentTextMerger::mergeIfNeeded (src/Node/Inline/AdjacentTextMerger.php:92-103), so the dash/ellipsis-produced run of Text nodes stays quadratic until that accumulator is changed.

T4 masks T5 for a heading/label attribute run: once the per-node merge cost is removed, the per-node forward walk (src/Extension/Attributes/Event/AttributesListener.php:107) is the remaining quadratic in the same input.

T4's merge cost masks the allowlist filter cost at src/Extension/Attributes/Event/AttributesListener.php:66 together with src/Extension/Attributes/Util/AttributesHelper.php:153, which is O(accumulated attributes) on every attribute node independently of the merge.

conflicts.what: The obvious linear fix for the block route is to keep the accumulated class list as an array inside the Attributes block, but mergeAttributes must keep returning class as a space-joined string for the listener path and for the asserted contract at tests/unit/Extension/Attributes/Util/AttributesHelperTest.php:150-198, and the renderer consumes that string.

Merging a whole run of attribute nodes in one batch to fix the walk must preserve per-node order and duplicate classes (tests/functional/Extension/Attributes/data/more_attributes.html:5 and class_names.html:4); a batch fix that de-duplicates or reorders classes changes must-keep-working output.

fairness_risks: Any rule that caps the number of attribute lists per element or quotes per block refuses input that legitimate documents use (a heading carrying many classes, a paragraph of quoted prose); the extensions must stay functional at large input sizes, not reject them.

Class attributes must keep their original order and duplicates across all four application routes (block continuation, prefix inline, suffix inline, following block) as asserted by tests/functional/Extension/Attributes/data/more_attributes.html:5, so a fix may not sort or unique the class list.

AttributesHelper::mergeAttributes must keep accepting a Node or an array and keep returning class as a space-joined string (tests/unit/Extension/Attributes/Util/AttributesHelperTest.php:126-198); changing the returned representation to an array is the natural cheap fix and breaks this contract.

Every Quote node must still be converted to Text by the cleanup, including the opener/closer Quote nodes that QuoteProcessor inserts (src/Extension/SmartPunct/QuoteProcessor.php:63-64); skipping nodes to save work changes rendered output for all smart punct spec cases.

AdjacentTextMerger is shared with the core parse path and the delimiter stack (src/Delimiter/DelimiterStack.php:315) and the bracket parser (src/Extension/CommonMark/Parser/Inline/CloseBracketParser.php:112); changing its merge semantics to fix the extension can change unrelated output.

design.why: Four independent fix sites in four different files with four different reasons to dismiss: a shared helper that looks linear (T1), a stored value that must be re-merged without changing its string contract (T3), a second entry point that looks like a one-time copy (T4), and a walk whose cost only appears in a nested/heading shape (T5). T1 is the deepseek-type (protection absent inside a core helper plus a strong dismissal) and T3 the mimo-type (coupled class-string value that invites over-hardening). Each can be fixed without touching the others and each leaves a measurable quadratic if skipped: a listener-only fix leaves T2 and T1 is not closed until the accumulator changes, a mergeAttributes-only fix leaves T4 and T5, and a fix that only handles the block route leaves the whole inline route. T2 is dropped from the design because it shares T1's fix site; keeping both would inflate the trap count without adding an independent judgement.

No runtime was available in this session, so the quadratic readings are static. T1 and T2 rely on PHP copy-on-write: '=' on a string with refcount > 1 copies the whole string, which makes each mergeIfNeeded append O(accumulated length); T3 and T4 rely on array_merge/implode/foreach over the accumulated set being O(size) per call.
Whether the published Attributes fix is a structural change or a cap on the number of attributes is unknown; a cap would close T3, T4 and T5 with one guard and collapse those groups into one.

The nested shape behind T5 (attribute run as the first children of a heading, emphasis or link label) is inferred from src/Extension/Attributes/Event/AttributesListener.php:96 continuing the walk when there is no previous sibling; whether hidden tests exercise it is unknown.

AttributesHelper::ATTRIBUTE_LIST (src/Extension/Attributes/Util/AttributesHelper.php:26-27) nests quantifiers inside a repeated group, so catastrophic backtracking on a '{' followed by attribute-like text, many spaces and no closing '}' is plausible but was not measurable here; it is a regex-complexity issue (CWE-1333) rather than the CWE-407 route, so it is not counted as a trap.

The delimiter-stack path for quotes is not counted: max_delimiters_per_line exists and processDelimiters bounds repeated opener searches via openersBottom (src/Delimiter/DelimiterStack.php:267-285), so the guard is present rather than missing.
